name: Muawiyah I Founds the Umayyad Caliphate
summary: After the assassination of Ali ibn Abi Talib, Muawiyah I of the Umayyad family becomes caliph, founding the first hereditary Islamic dynasty and moving the capital from Medina to Damascus. His secular-style governance and bureaucratic efficiency expand Islamic rule but alienate the pious who see the caliphate as departing from prophetic precedent.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Umayyad caliphate transforms Islam from a tribal confederation into a multi-ethnic empire; Damascus's location accelerates the adoption of Byzantine administrative techniques; the hereditary succession creates the Sunni-Shia split over legitimacy.
